description: Run 6C — resolving four concealed copies by TILE COUNT, not by asking the player. A winning hand is 14 tiles plus one for every kong, so whether a held quad is a concealed kong or a pong-plus-a-floater is decided by how many tiles the hand has. Written from the counting rule before the resolver existed.

cite.singapore: TT SS-Hand Structure (v1 reference) / TT SS-Eighteen Arhats: each kong adds one tile to the hand, so a winning hand is 14 + (number of kongs) tiles.
cite.hongkong: Hong Kong Old Style hand structure: the winning hand is 14 tiles, and each kong draws a replacement so a hand carrying k kongs is 14 + k tiles. The engine's own kong corpus (src/engine/corpus/hongkong/12-kongs.json, 'Hand sizes 14 to 18, and what a kong does and does not change') is written from Family A 香港蔴雀食糊牌型 / Family C 香港麻雀協會 official rules and is the archived source for it. NOT RULING HK1, which fixes the 144-tile SET.

entries.title: Four 1m at FOURTEEN are a pong and a chow, not a kong
entries.why: 1m 1m 1m 1m 2m 3m decomposes as 111m + 123m. The hand is already fourteen tiles and already reads, so nothing is a kong and the target stays fourteen. This is the case the Run 6 chip got wrong by growing the target the moment a fourth copy appeared.

entries.title: The same four tiles at FIFTEEN can only be a concealed kong
entries.why: Fifteen tiles cannot be four sets and a pair. The only reading is 1111m as a concealed kong plus 234m, so the quad IS a kong and the target is fifteen.

entries.title: A quad that cannot be a pong plus a floater asks for a fifteenth tile
entries.why: At fourteen these tiles do not decompose: 111m leaves a bare 1m that joins nothing. The resolver must therefore raise the target to fifteen so the wall accepts the tile the kong reading needs — the dead end Run 6 existed to remove, reached without ever asking the player.

entries.title: Two concealed kongs reach SIXTEEN
entries.why: Two quads that both have to be kongs put the hand two tiles above the base fourteen. Both are shown as kongs and the target is sixteen.

entries.title: Fifteen tiles holding TWO quads read exactly one of them as a kong
entries.why: One tile above the minimum means exactly one kong. The other quad is a pong plus a tile that joins a chow — 9s 9s 9s as a pong with the fourth 9s in 789s.

entries.title: An EXPOSED kong already declared does not make the held quad a kong too
entries.why: The declared kong has moved four tiles out of the concealed hand and raised the minimum to fifteen concealed-plus-meld. The remaining held quad is judged on its own by the same counting rule.

entries.title: Below the minimum, the target is the minimum and nothing is resolved yet
entries.why: A hand still being keyed is not a resolution question. Four copies held at eight tiles say nothing about kongs, and the target must not jump ahead of the player.

entries.title: Sixteen tiles that are not a hand stop asking for tiles
entries.why: At the ceiling the resolver must stop growing the target, so the screen says 'not a hand' rather than asking for a seventeenth tile the wall would refuse.

keyOrder.description: THE SAME TILES, KEYED IN ANY ORDER, MUST RESOLVE AND SCORE IDENTICALLY. A player keys a hand tile by tile in whatever order they pick it up; the resolver reads a multiset and must never depend on the sequence of taps.

cases.title: Four copies that are NOT a kong, at fourteen
